summary: Defines a Management Information Base, using SMIv2, for managing Classical IP and ARP over ATM. It lets network management tools monitor and configure that service. It is on the standards track.

eli5.summary: A checklist of dials and gauges that a network manager can read to see how a special kind of network connection is doing.

questions: classical ip and arp over atm management objects
what is a logical ip subnet
default mtu for ip over atm
subtitle: The SNMP management objects for watching and configuring Classical IP and ARP over ATM.

tldr.problem: Classical IP and ARP over ATM adds subnets, ATMARP servers and virtual circuits that the standard IP and interface MIBs cannot describe, so network managers had no way to monitor or configure them with SNMP.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 2320 defines the IPOA-MIB, an SMIv2 module split into basic, client and server groups of tables that tie each logical IP subnet, ATMARP server and virtual circuit to the existing IP and interface tables.
tldr.outcome: Every client and ATMARP server must support the basic group, clients add the ATMARP client table, and servers add the ATMARP server table plus notifications, so management stations can inspect and control the service in a uniform way.

today: RFC 2320 is a Proposed Standard published in April 1998. It has not been obsoleted or updated according to its metadata.

sections.title: Why an IPOA MIB
sections.content:
RFC 2320 is a product of the Internetworking Over NBMA Working Group. It defines a MIB module that extends the MIBs a normal TCP/IP system already supports, so that Classical IP and ARP over ATM can be managed. The module is written with the SMI for SNMP version 2.

The memo leans on several other documents. RFC 2011 (the IP group) is described as essential background, RFC 2233 (the Interfaces Group MIB) adds enhancements that help with ATM interfaces, and RFC 1695 (the ATM-MIB) is REQUIRED for the layers between AAL5 and ATM. The ATM Forum ILMI MIB is out of scope.
sections.eli5: Imagine a toy train set that comes with its own special pieces. This memo is the extra page in the manual that tells you how to check and set up those special pieces.

sections.title: How the MIB Is Organised
sections.content:
The MIB has three parts: Basic Support, Client Supported and Server Supported definitions. All IP and ARP over ATM entities, clients and ATMARP servers alike, are REQUIRED to support the basic part. Clients additionally support the client part, and ATMARP servers MUST additionally support the server part.

The MIB assumes the ATM-MIB layering of an ATM interface is in place and makes no assumption about how a system implements it. Several tables need an ifIndex that points to an ATM interface. A virtual IP over ATM interface layer is not required, but IANA created the ifType ipOverAtm(114) for systems that want one, and the IF-MIB ifStackTable SHOULD be used to show how such virtual interfaces relate to the physical ATM layers.
sections.eli5: The gauges are sorted into three boxes: one every machine must have, one for ordinary users of the network, and one for the machine that keeps the address book.

sections.title: Subnets, Servers and Circuits
sections.content:
The basic group has five tables and some notifications. The LIS table lists the logical IP subnets the system belongs to and is indexed by subnet address (ipoaLisSubnetAddr). Most of its objects control ATMARP for that subnet: inactivity timer, minimum holding time, queue depth, maximum calls, cache entry age, retries and timeout. ipoaLisMaxCalls caps the number of VCs per LIS, and ipoaLisDefaultMtu is the default MTU, which is not the same as the MTU actually negotiated for a circuit.

The LIS interface mapping table maps a subnet to every ATM interface that supports it. The ATMARP remote server table holds the configured remote ATMARP servers per subnet and interface. The ATM VC table has one entry for each VC per ATM interface per destination IP address, and records whether it is an SVC or PVC, the negotiated encapsulation and the negotiated MTU.

Setting ipoaLisRowStatus from active to notInService or destroy flushes the ATMARP cache for that subnet and removes the related VC entries.
sections.eli5: One list says which neighbourhoods you belong to. Another says which address-book keepers you can ask. A third lists every phone line currently open, and how big a message it can carry.

sections.title: Permanent Circuits
sections.content:
To use a permanent virtual circuit (PVC) for IP, a management station first creates the PVC with the ATM-MIB and then configures it for IP in the ATM Config PVC table. The VC table entry appears once the InATMARP reply arrives and reveals the IP address at the far end.

That entry gets type pvc(1), encapsulation llcSnap(1) and, by default, an MTU of 9180 octets. Classical IP and ARP over ATM allows other PVC MTU values but treats choosing one as out of scope; ipoaConfigPvcDefaultMtu can set it, and both ends MUST use the same value. The related ARP cache entry SHOULD be deleted when a PVC becomes unusable.
sections.eli5: A permanent circuit is a phone line that is always connected. The manager sets it up, and the other end says who it is, then both sides agree how long a message can be.

sections.title: Client and Server Tables
sections.content:
The only extra table a client MUST implement is the ATMARP client table. It shares its index (ipAdEntAddr) with the IP address table, holds the local ATM address and the ATMARP server in use, and counts InATMARP and ATMARP requests, replies and NAKs in both directions.

InATMARP retransmission is left to local policy. For a request over an SVC the memo suggests a timeout of 60 seconds with a retry count of 3, while over a PVC the retry limit may need to be infinite.

ATMARP servers MUST support the ATMARP server table, which lists the servers in a LIS and their statistics, and three notifications: ipoaDuplicateIpAddress, ipoaLisCreate and ipoaLisDelete. Both clients and servers MUST support ipoaMtuExceeded, sent when a frame larger than the negotiated MTU arrives. Create and delete notifications are controlled by ipoaLisTrapEnable.
sections.eli5: Each user keeps a tally of the questions it asked and the answers it got. The address-book keeper also rings a bell when two people claim the same address, or when a new neighbourhood appears.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
Some of this management information may be sensitive, so authentication of SNMP requests and controlled access SHOULD be used where that matters. The method comes from the SNMP Administrative Framework and is not extended by this MIB.

Several objects allow writes or row creation, which in a non-secure environment can harm network operations. The RFC RECOMMENDS that without at least authentication of the request origin, a list of objects be implemented read-only. The list includes ipoaLisDefaultMtu, ipoaLisInactivityTimer, ipoaLisMaxCalls, ipoaArpClientAtmAddr and ipoaConfigPvcDefaultMtu.
sections.eli5: Some of the dials could mess things up if a stranger turned them. So unless you know who is asking, the dials should be look-only.
